clue.text: Weapon of antiquity put on battlefield

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms
something of antiquity is old, aged
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: An ancient weapon is set down on the field of battle, as if in a museum display.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the biblical site of the final battle, hence any scene of catastrophic conflict.

clue.text: Dish, very dry, needs dipping in port

indicators.note: the very dry letters dip into the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
so means very, as in 'so tired'
TT is teetotal, which is dry

explanation.surface: A dish that is very dry needs to be soaked in port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' is the city Rio, not the fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock, an example of a dish.

clue.text: Singer's built stage without wings

indicators.note: the wings are the outer letters of the combined words, removed

parts.note: made means built, constructed
a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: A vocalist has erected a stage that has no wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer's' is 'Singer is', the 's a link. Adele is the London-born pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: The English singer-songwriter famous for 'Someone Like You' is an example of a singer.

clue.text: Aquatic bird — it nested in estuary's banks for aeons

definitions.note: plural in the clue, but 'for aeons' means for an endless time

indicators.note: a bird nesting sits within, so the pieces go inside
the banks of a river are its edges, so only the outer letters of estuary

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A seabird has made its nest on the banks of an estuary, where it has been for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's on 'estuary's' is just the possessive: the banks belong to the estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeons are immeasurably long ages; 'for aeons' and 'for all time' both mean an endless span.

clue.text: Leave, then enter most unmanageable shop

parts.note: to depart is to leave

indicators.note: out of control, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to go, then to push into the most chaotic shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unmanageable' rearranges ENTERMOST into MENTSTORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A large shop divided into sections selling different kinds of goods.

clue.text: French Marshal comes to harm getting Brazilian forward

parts.note: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals
to mar is to spoil or harm

explanation.surface: A French military officer is injured trying to stop a Brazilian attacker.
explanation.walkthrough: Neymar is the Brazilian footballer, a striker.
explanation.definitionFit: Neymar Jr is a famous Brazilian football striker, so a forward from Brazil.

clue.text: Nobleman from Balmoral or Dinnet?

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows, so they come from within it

explanation.surface: Asks whether an aristocrat hails from Balmoral or from Dinnet, two places on Royal Deeside in Aberdeenshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' signals letters lying inside 'BalmoraL OR Dinnet'. Balmoral is the royal castle in Scotland and Dinnet a nearby village.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer of the realm is addressed by this title, the general word for a male aristocrat.

clue.text: Oriental naughtily squeezing married circus performer

indicators.note: the rearranged letters squeeze the abbreviation into their middle
behaving naughtily, the letters misbehave and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An Eastern performer is mischievously hugging a married colleague in the circus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughtily' rearranges ORIENTAL into LIONTAER, and 'squeezing' takes M inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus act who controls big cats in the ring is a performer under the big top.

clue.text: Bloody judge imprisoning old Nick Timothy?

parts.note: red is the colour of blood, so bloody

indicators.note: the judging word locks the abbreviation for old inside it

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it

explanation.surface: A savage judge jails a former political adviser named Nick Timothy.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Timothy, Theresa May's adviser, was associated with Red Toryism, a Conservative strand with communitarian leanings; the question mark marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Timothy was a prominent example of the communitarian Conservative tendency, so he fits the label.

clue.text: Man being one in passageway losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the word for passageway drops its first letter

parts.note: an aisle is a passageway between seats

explanation.surface: Pictures a man standing in a corridor and somehow losing his head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person: it is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea, so 'Man being one' defines an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an example of an island, a small piece of land surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Rhetoric WS implies?

parts.note: the two letters W and S are what remains of a longer term once everything between its first and last letters is taken out

explanation.surface: Wonders what the initials WS are meant to suggest, like a puzzling monogram.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the inside of WORDS and only WS is left; so WS is what an emptied version of that term looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric in the pejorative sense is talk that sounds impressive but means nothing, hollow speech.

clue.text: Scattered right around in all directions

indicators.note: the turned letters go inside the compass points

parts.note: the four compass points south, east, west and north, abbreviated S, E, W, N

indicators.note: turned around, so the abbreviation for right is read backwards

explanation.surface: Something has been flung everywhere, right round in every direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all directions' is the four compass points, here taken in the order S, E, W, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Things spread untidily over a surface have been scattered there, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Response from corps joining battle

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
action means fighting, a battle

explanation.surface: An army unit replies by entering the fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply or answer to a stimulus is a synonym, as in 'what was her response?'

clue.text: Corbynites value Greek character making return

parts.note: moment means importance or value, as in 'of great moment'

indicators.note: making a return means the Greek letter is read backwards

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Supporters of Jeremy Corbyn prize a Greek figure who makes a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the grassroots campaign group formed in 2015 to back Jeremy Corbyn as Labour leader.

clue.text: Laurel perhaps remaining fresh and vital

definitions.meaning: a laurel is a shrub that keeps its leaves all year, one example of such plants
of a song or performer, never ageing or going out of fashion

explanation.surface: A laurel bush stays healthy and full of life.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names plants that keep their leaves year-round and anything that stays perennially popular.

clue.text: Con leading lady with answer that's illusion

parts.note: Theresa May, the female leader of the Conservatives (Con) at the time

explanation.surface: A con trick involving a lead actress and an answer turns out to be a mirage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' looks like a swindle, but it is short for Conservative; the leading lady is the party's then leader, Theresa May.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu philosophy maya is the illusory nature of the material world.

clue.text: Hairstyle and coronet adjusted by page

indicators.note: a coronet adjusted on the head is shifted around, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hairdo and a small crown are both straightened by a royal page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' turns CORONET into ETONCRO. The Eton crop is a short, slicked 1920s women's haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, boyish women's cut fashionable in the 1920s, an example of a hairstyle.

clue.text: Giant blunder on field disheartened Robespierre

parts.note: OG is an own goal, a football blunder on the pitch

indicators.note: with its heart taken out, only the ends of the name are left

explanation.surface: A huge mistake on the battlefield leaves the French revolutionary Robespierre dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' leaves only R and E of Robespierre.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy-tale monster of enormous size, so a giant in folklore.

clue.text: Brutal sort heading for real trouble enters Indian province

indicators.note: the first letter and the trouble go into the province's name

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: ill means trouble, as in 'speak no ill'

explanation.surface: A violent type, bound for serious trouble, arrives in an Indian region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' takes R from 'real'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorilla, informally, is a big brutish thug, a violent man.

clue.text: Fruitcake taken by PM recently shows dark colour

parts.note: a fruitcake, like a nut, is slang for a crazy person
Gordon Brown was British Prime Minister from 2007 to 2010

explanation.surface: A recent Prime Minister is handed a fruitcake, and something dark appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitcake' is the slang for a madman, not the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep shade like that of a ripe hazelnut shell, a darkish hue.

clue.text: British statesman getting stick after defence cut

indicators.note: the stick follows the shortened defence
cut short, so the defence loses its last letter

parts.note: a wall is a defensive barrier
a pole is a long stick

explanation.surface: A British politician is given a beating with a stick once his protection is withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims WALL to WAL. Sir Robert Walpole is generally regarded as Britain's first Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Walpole led British governments for two decades from 1721, a leading statesman.

clue.text: Secretary invites others round for meal

indicators.note: inviting someone in, so these letters take the secretary inside
the others go round the secretary, enclosing her letters

parts.note: the rest are the others
a PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: An office secretary invites colleagues over to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal word for a meal or the food eaten at one.

clue.text: Blairites' voting system used by female 17

definitions.note: the clue's possessive points to the group belonging to the Blairites

parts.note: PR is proportional representation
17 across is a giant; a female one is an ogress

explanation.surface: A Blairite electoral system is adopted by a female monster.
explanation.walkthrough: Progress was a Labour pressure group of Tony Blair's New Labour wing.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the New Labour think tank and pressure group associated with supporters of Tony Blair.

clue.text: Get to the point

definitions.meaning: to get to someone is to annoy or irritate them, to provoke them
a sharp sewing pin is all point, the slender pointed tool itself

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to irritate someone; as a noun it is a fine pointed sewing implement.

clue.text: One in swivel to have women going nuts?

definitions.text: One in swivel to have women going nuts?

indicators.note: the letters of swivel go crazy once the women's letter leaves, ending up rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone gyrating to drive the women wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going nuts' scrambles SWIVEL once W (women) has gone, leaving the letters of ELVIS. Elvis Presley's swivelling hips sent female fans wild.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley, nicknamed 'the Pelvis' for his gyrating hips, sent female fans into hysteria.

clue.text: Dirty work identifies party faction

parts.note: blue means smutty or dirty, as in blue jokes
labour is work

explanation.surface: Grubby toil is what marks out a group within a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue Labour is a socially conservative tendency in the British Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A named tendency within the British Labour Party, so a faction of that party.

clue.text: Sextet look round for something to play

parts.note: a sextet is six, VI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: turning round means the word for look is read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word for look

explanation.surface: A group of six musicians look around for music to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look' is the archaic 'lo', as in 'lo and behold'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Renaissance bowed string instrument, so something a musician plays.

clue.text: Man on board gets wife into god

indicators.note: the wife's letter is placed into the god's name

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A sailor on deck takes his wife to worship a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' is a chess piece on a chessboard, not a crewman.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess pieces are often called men, and the humblest of them is the foot soldier.

clue.text: Rook going after second ball in tree finds intruder

indicators.note: the rook's letter comes after the rest
the second and the pass sit inside the tree

parts.note: a ball in football is a pass to a teammate
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A rook, chasing a second ball lodged in a tree, turns out to be a trespasser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts SPASS inside TREE, giving TRESPASSE; 'going after' adds R at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who goes onto land without permission is an intruder there.
